entries.claim: This setting prints the 20-word postcommunio proper w001–w020, followed by the distinct abbreviated cue “Per Dóminum.” The full supplied ending and Amen are not printed at this proper locus. This is the May16 continuation before the explicit May17 heading, not a May17 prayer.

locator.section: RG115a complete ending and Amen wording; same-edition accented common stem and terminal typography

entries.claim: RG115a supplies the Father-directed Per Dominum ending w021–w041 and Amen w042. Its literal rubric formula is unaccented. Same-edition p.123 controls matching accented formula words, and p.226 controls the accented four-word terminal and separately marked Amen period. These controls do not make the proper page a full-ending witness or establish response actors, singing, or larger-group conclusion distribution.

locator.section: RG115a; this setting’s full ending and Amen

entries.claim: This setting’s own RG115a supplies its complete ad-patrem ending and Amen, w021–w042. Its literal accents, punctuation and Amen list semicolon are retained. Formula wording alone does not establish response actors, singing or a rule for grouped orations.
